method: WebSearch/WebFetch only, secondary sources; no primary-page fetches succeeded for OpenAI GitHub or Science paper

developments.who: OpenAI (unreleased internal model; advisory group at IAS)
developments.what: Bulk release in openai/math GitHub repo: 722 manuscripts in 372 result families (from ~4,000 attempted problems per README; ~3 GPU-hours/solution avg). Lean: top-level formalization ratio 300/719 (~42%, 'about half'); README warns unformalized results may be wrong. Examples: zeta zero-free regions, partial BSD, partial Hodge for CM abelian varieties, Hilbert-Smith, claimed Hadwiger disproof, integer-multiplication claim.
developments.why: Largest single AI-math claim dump; tests community verification capacity
developments.caveat: Counts vary by outlet (377 vs 372 vs 722); model/prompts not released; not independently replicated

developments.who: OpenAI; checked by Radziwill (NYU), Dunn (Georgia Tech); Sarnak teaching it
developments.what: 'Quasi-Riemann hypothesis': zeros in strip 1/8..7/8 (199pp, Lean-verified) and 1/12..11/12 (49pp, human-edited, not Lean-verified). Uses metaplectic forms and a 2021 Dunn-Radziwill formula.
developments.why: First widely reported expert acceptance of an AI-originated major analytic number theory result; full RH (1/2) still far
developments.caveat: Experts say papers poorly written; Sarnak will not call it a theorem until humans check details

developments.what: Three manuscripts withdrawn (sign error in 'stabilization trace' argument; algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds plus two dependents: Kuga-Satake for K3, rational Hodge for products of K3); 14 revised with proof repairs, 13 citation-only updates. None of the three were Lean-formalized.
developments.why: Concrete retraction data point; shows unformalized claims fail
developments.caveat: Secondary analysis blog; notice says proof failed, not that statement is false

developments.who: Bastounis, Circelli, Hansen (Cambridge), arXiv 'Navier-Stokes lost in translation'
developments.what: Argue OpenAI's Navier-Stokes Lean code is not a faithful translation of the paper (e.g. assumes m+5 derivatives vs m+4; different pressure-flux route), so a green Lean build does not certify the paper's proof.
developments.why: Challenges Lean-verified as a trust signal; the Sept 8 forced Navier-Stokes claim remains disputed
developments.caveat: Cited via blog; arXiv ID not retrieved

developments.what: Peer-reviewed publication of AlphaProof Nexus: 9 of 353 selected Erdos problems solved (two open 56 years) and 44 of 492 open OEIS conjectures, Lean-checked proofs released.
developments.why: Rare peer-reviewed, Lean-backed result with explicit denominators
developments.caveat: Independent audit says one of nine already implied by earlier theorem; a simpler agent reportedly solved the same nine

developments.who: Association for Human Mathematics open letter; Buckmaster, Sutherland, Tao, Litt
developments.what: Community response: AHM urges mathematicians not to collaborate with OpenAI; Buckmaster says plagiarism due diligence inadequate; Sutherland says unverified until model released; Tao calls for 'Math 2.0'; Litt calls results 'great for mathematics'. Advisory group said OpenAI followed only some disclosure recommendations.
developments.why: Governance and norms for AI claims

context_outside_window: 2026-09-08 OpenAI forced Navier-Stokes claim (166pp + Lean, ~$22M compute reported) disputed; credit dispute with Buckmaster/Alpoge

overhyped.claim: OpenAI solved a Millennium Prize problem (Navier-Stokes)
overhyped.reason: Result is for the forced equation with a smooth external force, not the unforced case; Scientific American reports three mathematicians say it dodges the question; Lean fidelity challenged; OpenAI says it will not seek the prize
Many are partial results; ~42% top-level Lean coverage; three withdrawn within a day; nothing replicated since the model is unreleased; counts inconsistent across outlets
Lean checks only the formal statement; statement-vs-intent and paper-vs-Lean fidelity gaps are documented

overhyped.claim: Quasi-RH as step toward Riemann Hypothesis
overhyped.reason: Several mathematicians doubt methods approach 1/2; the 11/12 paper is not Lean-verified
9 of 353 (~2.5%), one reportedly already implied by prior theorem, simpler agent matches it

unverified_note: Facts come from secondary outlets; primary pages (OpenAI GitHub, Science, arXiv) were not directly fetched.
